title: Fund governance, accounting and portfolio disclosures
objectives: Explain the oversight roles of trustees and the AMC.
Describe NAV accounting and the regular disclosures.
body_md:
## Checks and balances

| Constituent | Role |
|---|---|
| **Sponsor** | Sets up the fund |
| **Trustees** | Hold the assets for unitholders, supervise the AMC; the board needs a majority of independent trustees |
| **AMC** | Manages the schemes; its board also has independent directors |
| **Custodian** | Safekeeps securities, separate from the AMC |
| **RTA** | Registrar and transfer agent for unit records |
| **Auditor** | Audits the schemes' accounts |

## NAV accounting

**NAV = (market value of investments + other assets − liabilities and expenses) ÷ units outstanding.**

- Investments are **marked to market** daily using approved valuation agencies for debt.
- Expenses accrue daily, so the NAV is already **net of the TER**.
- Income is booked on an accrual basis.

## Regular disclosures

- NAV published **every business day**.
- **Portfolio** disclosed monthly and half-yearly; the **riskometer** reviewed monthly.
- Half-yearly financial results and an **annual report** are available to every unitholder.
- Liquidity **stress tests** for open-ended debt schemes, and swing pricing rules where applicable (verify the current circulars).

## Why it protects investors

The assets sit with the **trustees and custodian**, not with the AMC, so an AMC failure does not remove the scheme assets.

> **Exam tip:** NAV is net of expenses; the custodian holds the securities.
